title: CLCON/273/2007 of GIRISH CHANDRA PATHAK Vs PROF. C.P. BARTHWAL AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Contempt Petition No. 273 of 2007
Girish Chandra Pathak ÖPetitioner
Versus
Prof. C. P. Barthwal, Vice Chancellor,
Kumaun University Nainital & another
 ÖRespondents
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. None present for the parties.
2. In the interest of justice, record has been perused.
In the present contempt petition there is an order dated
8.1.2004 of the learned Single Judge of this Court passed
in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2 of 2004. The operative portion
of the order reads as under:-
 ìIn the meantime, it is provided that in
case the post has been sanctioned by the State
Government and the State Government has released
the budget for payment of salary in favour of the
petitioner and if the petitioner is working, the
arrears of salary shall be paid to the petitioner and
the termination order shall be treated to be in
abeyance so far as the petitioner is concerned. The
respondents are directed to show cause as to why
the salary has not been paid to the petitioner.î
3. It is this order, which is alleged to have been
violated. However, from the record of the present
contempt petition, it is found that the said writ petition
has already been dismissed by a Division Bench of this
Court on 23.6.2011. The operative portion of the order
reads as under:-
 ìIn the circumstances, the
Government did not create any post, where the
petitioner could be regularized. Furthermore,
at no point of time, the University acquired any
authority, either from the legislature or from
the administrators, to regularize a person,

2
associated with a research project, in a post
created with the University. That being the
situation, the conclusion in the instant case
would be identical, as concluded by us in the
writ petition referred to above. The writ
petition stands dismissed.î
4. As such, the writ petition has been dismissed on
merits by Division Bench of this Court. Nothing has been
brought on record as to how and under what
circumstances contempt has been committed. More
particularly the writ petition has itself been dismissed.
Therefore, no contempt is made out.
5. The contempt petition is hereby dismissed.
6. Notices are also hereby discharged.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 06.03.2012
Kuldeep
